Lets Telos Launcher suspend and hide other apps to save battery, once granted device owner status via adb. Only takes effect after the one-time setup in Freeze settings → Device Owner.

Device owner status gives this app deep control over the device and is hard to undo - typically only a factory reset, short of removing it the same way it was granted. Only set this up if you understand what device owner mode means and are comfortable running adb commands.

It can only be granted on a device with no Google account, work profile, or existing device/profile owner already set up. If this device already has accounts on it, remove them first (Settings → Accounts) - you can add them back afterward, this only blocks the one-time setup, not normal use once it\'s done.
1. Connect this device to a computer with adb and enable USB debugging (Settings → Developer options).
2. Run this exact command from that computer:
3. Come back here and check the status below - it should say \"Device owner is active\".
I understand the risks and requirements above

Run this command from a computer to give up device owner status (works on most Android versions; if it fails, a factory reset is the fallback). Any accounts you removed for setup can be added back immediately after, whether you undo this or not.
Even as device owner, this app can only suspend and hide apps - it cannot force-stop them or clear their cache. Use Shizuku or root for those.
